Landmark-normalised time columns

Source: R/landmarks.R
normalise_time_landmarks.Rd

Puts each segment of a landmark set, such as each syllable, on its own 0-1 time axis that runs from the segment's first f0 to its last f0, so contour shapes can be compared. Adds three columns, named from the set:

  • <set>_t01: 0 at the segment's first f0 and 1 at its last f0.

  • <set>_tseq: the segments in sequence, (<set>_i - 1) + <set>_t01. Segment 1's f0 fills 0 to 1, segment 2's fills 1 to 2, and so on. A stretch without f0 between two segments, such as a voiceless consonant at a syllable boundary, takes no room, so every boundary sits at a whole number: segment 1's last f0 and segment 2's first f0 are both at 1.

  • <set>_tbound: the segments in sequence, gap kept: they meet at the TextGrid boundaries, and the stretch without f0 between them is kept. The boundaries between the token's segments are at 1, 2, .... Its first f0 is at 0 and its last f0 at n, the number of segments. A segment with no f0 at all at the token's start or end gets NA, so the token then starts at 1 (or ends at n - 1), and its boundaries still line up with other tokens'. A stretch without f0 at a boundary keeps its length, split at the boundary between the segments on either side.

Usage

normalise_time_landmarks(df, time, set, f0 = "f0", token = "token")

Arguments

df

Data frame with the time, f0 and token columns and the set's <set>_start and <set>_end columns (and usually <set>_i), as from attach_landmarks().

time

Name of the time column.

set

Landmark-set prefix (e.g. "syllable").

f0

Name of the f0 column that says which rows have f0. Default "f0". For F0 Correction output, pass f0 = "f0_corrected": left at the default, the tracked f0 would decide, with a message.

token

Name of the token-ID column. Default "token". With time counted within each token, two tokens can have the same boundary values, so segments are always taken within a token.

Value

df with <set>_t01 added (or replaced), and <set>_tseq and <set>_tbound when df has a <set>_i column. Without <set>_i, these two are not added, with a message. A missing column is an error.

Details

A segment is one interval of the tier within one token: the rows that share the token and the <set>_start and <set>_end values that attach_landmarks() wrote. On <set>_t01 and <set>_tseq, the boundaries only say which rows belong to which segment, and the axis comes from where f0 is. On <set>_tbound, the boundaries between segments also set the whole numbers: segment i runs from i - 1 to i, from its start boundary to its end boundary, except that the token's first segment with f0 starts at its first f0 and its last segment with f0 ends at its last f0. Only labelled segments count, as in contour_duration() with set, so rows in an empty-label interval (silence), rows outside the tier and rows with no token get NA.

A row has f0 when its f0 value is a number. In a column in Hz (one that hz_f0_columns() finds), 0 is no f0. A column with negative markers, such as -1, is not read as Hz, so those values count as f0: set them to NA first (see suggest_unvoiced()). In a signed or normalised column, such as semitones or z-scores, 0 and negative values are f0.

Rows without f0 between a segment's first and last f0 keep their place by time. Rows before the first f0 or after the last get NA, not 0 or 1, and so does every row of a segment with f0 at fewer than two times. On <set>_tbound the same holds for the token as a whole: rows before its first f0 or after its last get NA, and so do segments with no f0 before its first segment with f0 or after its last. A segment with no f0 between two segments with f0 keeps its place, from boundary to boundary. When only one segment of a token has f0, its <set>_tbound equals its <set>_tseq. So removing rows without f0, or reordering the rows, does not change any of the three columns.

Two rows at each boundary. On <set>_tseq, segment 1's last f0 and segment 2's first f0 are both at 1, so the axis has two rows at each whole number, often with different f0. compute_mean_contour() and cluster_features() read the next segment's first f0 at the boundary, and never average the two. They tell the two rows apart by <set>_t01 (1 on the last f0, 0 on the first) or <set>_i, so the row order does not matter while either column is kept. For fit_gamm(), whose AR1 correction runs along the rows, keep the rows in time order within each token. On <set>_tbound the stretch without f0 keeps its room, so a whole number has a row only where a row sits exactly on a boundary.

Modelling a whole word. One smooth over <set>_tseq, as in fit_gamm(), cannot follow an f0 jump at a boundary: both sides of it are at the same time. On <set>_tbound the two sides are a gap apart, so one smooth can follow the jump, and the boundaries still line up across tokens. token_t01 from normalise_time_token() keeps the gap too, but the boundary falls at a different point in each token. Or model each segment on <set>_t01, with one token per segment.

The first and last f0 are taken as they are: a lone sample cut off from the rest of the segment's contour by a gap counts. contour_duration() instead anchors its span on runs of at least min_run = 2 samples by default, so the two can disagree about such a segment. The Start page's option for short edge runs, or drop_rows_without_f0(min_run = 3), removes such samples first, but only at a token's start and end: a lone sample next to a boundary inside the token still sets that segment's 0 or 1.

For <set>_t01 and <set>_tseq, only the order and spacing of time within a segment matter, so the time column does not have to be in the TextGrid's units. <set>_tbound compares time with the boundaries, so it needs time, <set>_start and <set>_end on the same clock: in the same units and counted from the same zero, as attach_landmarks() writes them. In a token with f0 in two or more segments whose time lies outside its own segments' boundaries (by more than a millionth of the token's time range), <set>_tbound is NA, with a message.

Columns made by shinytone 1.0.0 ran from each interval's start boundary to its end boundary. Make them again with this function.

See also

normalise_time_token() for the whole token, which for a word keeps the gap between syllables and their duration ratio; contour_duration() with set for the duration of the same segments.

Examples

# Two syllables, with no f0 at the boundary
df <- data.frame(token = "w1", time = seq(0.01, 0.10, by = 0.01),
                 f0 = c(NA, 200, 205, 210, NA, NA, 190, 185, 180, NA),
                 syllable_start = rep(c(0, 0.05), each = 5),
                 syllable_end   = rep(c(0.05, 0.11), each = 5),
                 syllable_i     = rep(1:2, each = 5))
out <- normalise_time_landmarks(df, "time", "syllable")
out[, c("time", "f0", "syllable_t01", "syllable_tseq", "syllable_tbound")]
#>    time  f0 syllable_t01 syllable_tseq syllable_tbound
#> 1  0.01  NA           NA            NA              NA
#> 2  0.02 200          0.0           0.0       0.0000000
#> 3  0.03 205          0.5           0.5       0.3333333
#> 4  0.04 210          1.0           1.0       0.6666667
#> 5  0.05  NA           NA            NA       1.0000000
#> 6  0.06  NA           NA            NA       1.2500000
#> 7  0.07 190          0.0           1.0       1.5000000
#> 8  0.08 185          0.5           1.5       1.7500000
#> 9  0.09 180          1.0           2.0       2.0000000
#> 10 0.10  NA           NA            NA              NA
# Removing the rows without f0 gives the same values
kept <- !is.na(df$f0)
identical(normalise_time_landmarks(df[kept, ], "time", "syllable")$syllable_tbound,
          out$syllable_tbound[kept])
#> [1] TRUE
